title: Atlas Approval
description: That a run needed a person's approval, and what was approved. Core decides `required` from the task; only a host sets the grant fields, through `atlas_core.approval.ApprovalAuthority` on a person's answer. This record permits nothing by itself: `ToolGateway.invoke_write` runs a write only on a single-use, expiring token for the exact operation, and re-checks the repository's commit before the handler. What the contract does is make a grant unstateable without saying what it is a grant OF. `granted: true` requires `binds_to`, whose `sha256` is the digest of the exact operation (tool, arguments, repository, ref and commit), so an approval is never a bare boolean that outlives the thing it approved. See docs/safety-model.md.

required.description: Whether this run may not finish without a person. Derived from the task by `requires_write_approval`, which the producer did not write.

reason.description: Why approval was required. `not_recorded` when the document this was migrated from did not keep one — a plausible sentence here would be indistinguishable from a recorded one.

granted.description: Null means nobody has answered. False means refused. True requires `binds_to`; only a host's `ApprovalAuthority` writes it.

granted_by.description: Who answered. Null when nobody has.

binds_to.description: What exactly was approved. Required when `granted` is true, because an approval that does not name its subject approves everything. The digest is what makes it expire: if the evidence changes, the approval no longer matches.
